subject: PO ID fallback / split-release invoice approach for Q3 commitment
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@starlakehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlakehealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID fallback / split-release invoice approach for Q3 commitment

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of clarification points from procurement as we prepare the PO:

• Our ERP requires a single PO ID per legal entity, but our accounting can accept up to three invoice releases tied to that single PO. Can you confirm Redwood will accept one PO ID with multiple invoice releases?

• Net terms: Our standard is Net45. We need to confirm Redwood will honor Net45 on the committed monthly tranche invoices. If there are any prepay requirements for reserved capacity, flag those explicitly.

• PO header fields: our AP team expects PO header to include BU code, cost center, and contract reference (format: SLH-RED-YYYY). Does your invoicing support freeform header fields or do you need a fixed mapping?

Attached is our PO format template (Starlake_PO_Format_Reqs.pdf) and a suggested split schedule.

Appreciate a short email we can attach to the PO stating Redwood accepts the single PO / multi-release approach.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager, Starlake Health
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@starlakehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID fallback / split-release invoice approach for Q3 commitment

Hi Dana —

Thanks — we can accommodate what you outlined. Summary for your AP team:

• Single PO ID: Confirmed. Redwood can accept one PO ID from Starlake and apply multiple invoice releases against that PO.

• Invoice releases: Up to three invoice releases tied to the single PO is fine. We typically surface the release number in the invoice reference (e.g., PO-12345 / Release 1).

• Net terms: We can invoice on a Net45 basis for the committed monthly tranche invoices. One caveat — any usage overages billed on the hosted API usage meter will be invoiced monthly on Net30 by default unless you request those to be batched into the tranche invoice (we can do that but need explicit signoff).

• PO header fields: We support freeform header fields and can map BU code, cost center, and the contract reference string to the invoice metadata. Please provide the exact field names your ERP expects; we will mirror them in our AR exports.

I've attached an example proposed split (Proposed_Invoice_Split.xlsx) that mirrors your suggested timing but keeps usage overage lines separate unless you request consolidation.

Next steps for closure:
1) Proc sends finalized PO template with exact header field names.
2) Starlake confirms whether usage overages should be consolidated into the tranche invoices or invoiced separately.
3) Once we have PO and confirmation, Redwood will provide a short acceptance note suitable to attach to the PO.

If you want, we can also insert a clause in the SOW stating Redwood acknowledges single-PO, multi-release invoicing for this engagement.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@starlakehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID fallback / split-release invoice approach for Q3 commitment

Quick add — commercial touchpoints on discounts and packaging:

• Pricing/Discounts: Starlake is qualifying for the Tier 2 volume band for reserved capacity (12–24 GPU-months). That band includes a 12% recurring discount off list for reserved compute + a 5% onboarding credit applied to the first tranche invoice.

• Packaging: We propose separating Reserved Capacity (committed) from Variable Usage (hosted API) on the invoice so your finance team can tie committed spend to the PO and variable spend to the usage account. This avoids ERP reclassification.

• Payment cadence: If the PO will be used for committed tranches only, we can accept Net45 on those invoices. For the onboarding credit, we can show it as a negative line on the first tranche invoice.

If procurement needs the 5% onboarding credit to appear as a separate credit memo instead, we can issue that post-first-invoice — let us know your preference.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if we need to get AP standards locked down today.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@starlakehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@starlakehealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID fallback / split-release invoice approach for Q3 commitment

Hannah / Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few confirmations from our side after internal review:

1) Single PO with up to three releases: confirmed. AP can map releases to the PO number and will accept Release X notation.

2) Net terms: Net45 on committed tranche invoices is acceptable. For monthly usage overages, please consolidate them into the tranche invoices — our preference is a single monthly charge per entity rather than separate AD-hoc invoices.

3) Header fields: Attached is the exact ERP field list (will send in separate email from AP). Please map "BU_CODE", "COSTCENTER", and "CONTRACT_REF" to the invoice metadata.

4) Onboarding credit: Please show the 5% onboarding credit as a negative line on Invoice Release 1 (no separate credit memo).

5) Final ask: Could Redwood produce a one-paragraph acceptance statement we can append to the PO that states: Redwood Inference accepts PO ID XYZ-2027 (single PO with multi-release invoices), will map BU and cost center fields, consolidate usage into tranche invoices, and invoice committed tranches on Net45.

We aim to issue the PO by EOD Friday if we receive the acceptance paragraph and the sample mapped invoice.

Best,
Dana
Sr. Procurement Manager, Starlake Health
